meta.title: Order Access: Enforce the Server Boundary
meta.subtitle: Replace client-controlled access checks with server-side least privilege and a hardened session cookie.

brief.role: You are reviewing a fictional guest-order API and its session helper.
brief.context: The UI hides the order view for most users, but the API is using a client-controlled value to make an authorization decision. Review the server boundary and the session cookie, then check for a similar gap in a support route.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. All account and order references are fictional. Do not include real guest data, session tokens or secrets in code, logs or AI prompts.

mission.objective: Enforce authorization on the server with least privilege and protect the session at the cookie boundary.

riskSignals.label: Order data not scoped to the signed-in guest
Support route lacks a server-side check

achievements.title: Access reviewer
achievements.description: Completed the mission without using a hint.

achievements.title: Boundary spotter
achievements.description: Recognized a missing server check in a second route.

files.content:

Guest route: server identity and resource scope now checked

feedbackByMissing.order-route:2: A UI-derived flag can be controlled outside the server's trusted identity and authorization boundary.

stages.title: Mark every line that weakens the access or session boundary
stages.instruction: Select the client-controlled authorization evidence and the session-cookie write that need correction.
hints: A hidden UI element or a value supplied in the request is not a server-side access control.
Check both the value used to decide access and the cookie options used for the session.

feedback.correct: You found the client-controlled authorization path and the session cookie without protective flags.
feedback.incorrect: Review what the server trusts to authorize the order and how the cookie is set.

feedbackByMissing.order-route:2: The requester can control this header or UI-derived value. It is not a trustworthy authorization attribute.
feedbackByMissing.order-route:4: This check enforces a client claim rather than the signed-in identity and its permitted resource scope.
feedbackByMissing.session-helper:2: A session cookie needs secure attributes so browser script cannot read it, it is HTTPS-only and cross-site sending is limited.

concept.label: Authorize sensitive actions on the server

stages.title: Select every control the correction requires
stages.instruction: Choose the controls that enforce least privilege and improve the session boundary.

choices.label: Use the authenticated server-side identity and permissions for the authorization decision
choices.feedbackIfMissed: A request header or UI state cannot stand in for the authenticated identity maintained by the server.

choices.label: Verify the requested order belongs to the authorized guest before returning it
choices.feedbackIfMissed: A valid sign-in alone does not authorize every order. Scope the resource to the least privilege needed.

choices.label: Set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite cookie flags with a short session lifetime
choices.feedbackIfMissed: The session boundary needs browser-enforced protections as well as a reasonable lifetime.

choices.label: Hide the order link for users who should not see it
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Hiding a UI element can improve the experience, but a caller can still invoke the endpoint directly. It is not the access control.

hints: Think about identity, resource ownership and the cookie boundary.
A complete correction puts authorization on the server and does not treat the UI as the enforcement point.

feedback.correct: The correction uses server-controlled identity and least-privilege resource checks, then hardens the session cookie.
feedback.incorrect: One or more selected controls leave authorization in the client or omit an important session protection.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Primary access controls applied · support-route finding requires review

concept.label: Grant and check only the access required for the resource

stages.title: Run the simulated access checks
stages.instruction: Verify the corrected guest route and cookie, then inspect the remaining route finding before clearing the review.

results.message: The route uses the signed-in identity, permission and order ownership to make its server-side decision.
The route still depends on a value the caller can control.
The session cookie includes HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite protections with a bounded lifetime.
The session cookie does not yet include the required protective options.
The support route returns an order without a server-side authorization and ownership check.

feedback.failed: The main route and cookie are safer, but verification found another endpoint that bypasses the same server boundary.

stages.title: Find the missing check in the support route
stages.instruction: Select the line that returns a sensitive resource without first confirming server-side permission and scope.
hints: The route must establish permission and resource scope before it sends an order.
Find the return path that has no server-side guard.

feedback.correct: You recognized that every sensitive endpoint needs its own server-side authorization check, even when another UI or route already appears protected.
feedback.incorrect: The unsafe line returns the order before the server confirms permission and resource ownership.

feedbackByMissing.support-route:2: This endpoint returns an order immediately. Add server-side permission and resource-scope checks before the response.

concept.label: Authorize sensitive actions on the server

completion.title: The server owns the authorization decision
completion.message: You moved access decisions to the server, scoped data to the signed-in guest, hardened the session cookie and caught a similar endpoint regression.
takeaways: A hidden UI element, client flag or request header is not an authorization control.
Check permission and resource ownership on the server for every sensitive action.
Use short-lived sessions and secure cookie flags: HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.
